## Security Review Summary

I scanned all 10 files in the repository (7 Python source files in `app/`, 2 HTML templates, 1 JS file). No dependency manifests exist, so no dependency audit was possible.

### Findings (2)

| Severity | ID | File(s) | Issue |
|----------|-----|---------|-------|
| 🔴 CRITICAL | `server-side-template-injection` | `app/rendering.py`, `app/routes.py` | User input (`name` query param) concatenated into Jinja2 template source via `render_template_string('Welcome ' + name)`. Attacker injects `{{...}}` syntax → info leak / RCE. |
| 🟠 HIGH | `cross-site-scripting` | `templates/profile.html`, `app/profile.py` | User-controlled `bio` form field rendered with `{{ bio\|safe }}`, disabling Jinja2 auto-escaping. The existing `sanitized_html()` bleach function exists but is **not used** on this path. |

### Verified SAFE (no findings — avoided false positives)
- **`app/db.py`** — parameterized `?` placeholder query; no SQL injection.
- **`app/redirects.py`** — allowlist validator requiring both `scheme=='https'` AND `hostname=='portal.example.test'`; no exploitable open redirect.
- **`app/config.py`** — `SECRET_KEY` read from environment, `DEBUG=False`; no hardcoded secret.
- **`app/security.py`** — strict `bleach.clean` allowlist (3 tags, no attributes); safe sanitizer (just unused on the profile path).
- **`static/comment.js`** — uses `textContent`, not `innerHTML`; DOM-safe.
- **`templates/account.html`** — relies on Jinja2 default auto-escaping; safe.

### Report
The machine-readable report was saved to **`SECURITY_REVIEW.json`** (validated as well-formed JSON). No audited source files were modified — `git diff` is empty and only the new `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` file is untracked.
